wine.name: Xinomavro Reserve Vieilles Vignes Single Block Barba Yannis
wine.grapes: Xinomavro alone, as the Amyndeon appellation requires for its red.
wine.sites: The Barba Yannis block, one parcel of ungrafted bush vines planted in 1919, at about 650 metres on the plateau, on sandy and sandy clay soils over limestone conglomerate that drain well and kept phylloxera out.
wine.making: By the house's sheets the grapes are destemmed and lightly crushed and given a cold soak on the skins of some days. Fermentation runs on yeasts isolated from the block itself, the temperature raised slowly. The wine then spends eighteen months to two years in French oak barrels, on its lees, and more time in bottle before release.
wine.glass: Dried cherry and dried rose over tobacco leaf, tomato leaf and a touch of leather; denser and darker than the estate's Hedgehog, with emphatic, firm tannin held up by the plateau's high, bright acidity.
wine.ageing: Firm and closed in its first years; it is made for the cellar, and a good vintage keeps its fruit and grip for well over a decade.
wine.serve: 16 to 18 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for an hour or more, an older one gently off its sediment; a Burgundy or Nebbiolo style glass.

records.table: Alpha Estate's Barba Yannis is Xinomavro from one block of ungrafted bush vines planted in 1919 on the sands of the Amyndeon plateau. Dried cherry, rose and tobacco leaf ride on firm tannin and cold climate acidity; decant it and pour it with lamb.
records.story: The vines are older than the estate. In 1919 a grower on the Amyndeon plateau planted a block of Xinomavro as bush vines on their own roots; the sandy soil here gives the phylloxera louse no hold, so the vines never needed grafting and survived the century. Alpha Estate was founded in 1997 by a viticulturist and an oenologist who, by the house's account, had worked across Greece and abroad before choosing the plateau, high and cold between four lakes, to make wine of their own. The estate planted a large vineyard of its own at over 600 metres, with Xinomavro beside Syrah, Merlot, Sauvignon Blanc and other grapes, and bought the old block from the descendants of its former owner, naming it Barba Yannis after him: uncle John, in the Greek manner of addressing an old man. The block's wine became the estate's old vine reserve, labelled over the years as Ecosystem, Reserve Vieilles Vignes and Single Block Barba Yannis, and fermented on yeasts the house isolated from the block. Amyndeon had been an appellation since 1972, known for rosé and the co-operative's wines; Barba Yannis showed what its old ungrafted Xinomavro could give as a red to cellar. For a sommelier it is the plateau's answer to Naoussa.

wine.name: Extra Cuvée de Réserve Zero Dosage
wine.appellation: Wine of Greece, grown on the Amyndeon plateau
wine.grapes: Xinomavro alone, from ungrafted vines: a blanc de noirs, white wine from a black grape.
wine.sites: The Rasto, Sotirtsko and Bella Toumba vineyards at about 650 metres, on soils of sand and clay, with ungrafted vines of sixty years and more, farmed organically by the house's account.
wine.making: Picked by hand in September and pressed as whole bunches in a basket press. The base wine ferments in foudres of twenty hectolitres with no sulphur and no additives, by the house's sheet, and is bottled the following winter for its second fermentation. It then rests five to seven years on its lees, is disgorged with no dosage and is held six months more before release.
wine.glass: Salt cured lemon peel and hay over underripe raspberry and pear skin, bone dry, with piercing acidity, a lively mousse and a firm, bitter grip from the black grape's skins that marks it apart from Champagne.
wine.ageing: Ready on release after its long years on the lees; its high acidity and lack of sugar let it keep for some years more.
wine.serve: 8 to 10 degrees Celsius; no decanting; a tulip or white wine glass rather than a narrow flute, to let it open.

label.means: The house's long aged, zero dosage blanc de noirs of old, ungrafted Xinomavro.

records.table: Domaine Karanika's Extra Cuvée de Réserve is a traditional method blanc de noirs of old, ungrafted Xinomavro from the Amyndeon plateau, rested five years and more on its lees with no dosage. Lemon peel, hay and a firm bite; pour it with oysters or cured fish.
records.story: In 2004, as the house tells it, a couple living in the Netherlands left their work to make organic sparkling wine by the traditional method, and went looking for a grape and a place to do it. They found Xinomavro, little known outside Greece, and the cold Amyndeon plateau, where sandy soils had kept old vines on their own roots and where the co-operative had tried sparkling wine of the grape since 1971. Domaine Karanika grew from there into a house devoted to sparkling wine, working plots in seven villages of the appellation, with Assyrtiko and Limniona beside its Xinomavro, and a gravity flow winery whose cellars, by its own account, hold some wines on their lees for up to twelve years. The Extra Cuvée de Réserve took old ungrafted vines of sixty years and more, pressed as whole bunches and fermented in large foudres, and gave them years on the lees with no sugar at the end. By the house's history, its listing at a New York restaurant in 2016 was a turning point for the range abroad. The 2017 vintage spent between four and a half and seven years on the lees. From the 2019 vintage the same old vine, zero dosage blanc de noirs appears as Cuvée Céleste. It is the reference for long aged sparkling Xinomavro.

wine.name: Amyndeon Rosé Dry
wine.grapes: Xinomavro alone, as the appellation requires for its rosé.
wine.sites: Poor, sandy hillside vineyards across the Amyntaio zone, grown by the co-operative's member farmers under integrated management, by the house's sheet.
wine.making: Xinomavro picked from the end of September is destemmed and crushed and left on its skins for only a few hours. The must is settled with enzymes, then fermented slowly with selected yeasts in tanks with automatic cooling, as a white wine would be, and bottled young.
wine.glass: Wild cherry in colour, with wild strawberry, fresh tomato and green olive on the nose; dry, light and crisp, with the high acidity the cold plateau gives every Xinomavro grown there.
wine.ageing: Made for freshness rather than the cellar: drink it in the year or two after the harvest.
wine.serve: 10 to 12 degrees Celsius, as the house advises; no decanting; a white wine glass.

records.table: The Amynteo co-operative's dry rosé is Xinomavro alone from the growers' sandy hillsides, in the one Xinomavro appellation that allows rosé. Wild strawberry, tomato and olive on a crisp, dry frame; pour it cool with grilled fish or a Florina pepper meze.
records.story: The co-operative came before the appellation. In 1945, by the house's own history, twenty seven village co-operatives of the district joined as the Union of Agricultural Cooperatives of Amyntaio, and in 1959 the union built a winery in the town, its main work from then on. Its first red came in 1960 and sold across Western Macedonia. Around 1971 the winery began trials of sparkling wine from Xinomavro, and when Greece drew up its first appellations in 1972, Amyntaio was recognised for red, rosé and sparkling wine of the grape alone. That made the plateau the one Xinomavro zone where rosé holds a place, and the house calls its rosé the only rosé PDO in Greece. The winery later passed to the Agricultural Cooperative of the Wider Amyntaio Area and trades as Amyntas Wines. Its range runs from sparkling rosés, dry and semi dry, to a dry rosé, a dry red and a red from selected high vineyards of old vines. For a sommelier the dry rosé is the plainest lesson in the appellation: the grape of Naoussa's long aged reds, here pressed after a few hours on its skins for a pale, sharp wine of the cold north.

records.table: Hatzis Winery's 7 Roots is a dry red of Xinomavro alone from the Amyntaio zone, aged a year on its fine lees in oak. Red currant, rose jam and sun dried tomato on sharp acidity and light tannin; pour it with grilled lamb chops or beans.
records.story: The family traded wine before the Second World War, as exporters and producers in the district, by the account of a Greek merchant's page on the house. Later a descendant, trained as a chemical engineer, set out to revive it: in 2000 he began making wine again from an old family vineyard of Amyntaio. The plateau had been an appellation since 1972, PDO Amyndeon, Xinomavro alone for red, rosé and sparkling wine. The house works with Xinomavro across its range: a red under the appellation, a rosé, and a white blanc de noirs, Dodekatos, fermented on wild yeasts and rested in oak on its lees, which stands outside the PDO as a wine of PGI Florina. 7 Roots is the house's PDO red as merchants in Greece and New York sell it, a dry Xinomavro given a year on its fine lees in oak. It is a small family house, known in Greece and little seen abroad, and for a sommelier it shows the plateau's Xinomavro in a lighter, sharper register than Naoussa, the appellation over the mountain to the east.

wine.name: Xinomavro
wine.grapes: Xinomavro alone, as the Amyndeon appellation requires for its red.
wine.sites: Vineyards of Agios Panteleimon beside Lake Vegoritida, on slopes running down from Mount Kaimaktsalan, among the plateau's four lakes of Vegoritida, Petron, Zazari and Chimaditida.
wine.making: By a Greek wine magazine's note on the 2019, the wine is aged twelve months in oak barrels and twelve more in bottle before release; the house's own account of the fermentation was not found.
wine.glass: In the manner of the plateau's Xinomavro: sour cherry and ripe tomato over olive and dried herbs, turning towards pepper with age; pale for a red, with sharp acidity and firm tannin.
wine.ageing: Released after two years, a year in oak and a year in bottle; it softens over a few years more.
wine.serve: 15 to 17 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for half an hour; a Burgundy glass.

label.means: The house's name, taken from Lake Vegoritida, beside which its vineyards lie.
The protected appellation of the Florina plateau, Xinomavro alone for red, rosé and sparkling wine.

records.table: Vegoritis Winery takes its name from the lake beside its vines at Agios Panteleimon, and its Xinomavro is a dry red of the grape alone under PDO Amyndeon, a year in oak and a year in bottle. Pour it cool for its sharp acidity, with lamb or peppers.
records.story: Agios Panteleimon is one of the wine villages of the Amyndeon plateau, the high, cold ground of Florina ringed by mountains and set among four lakes. Its growers had sent their grapes for generations to the co-operative in Amyntaio town, whose winery opened in 1959, and when Greece drew up its first appellations in 1972 the plateau became PDO Amyndeon, Xinomavro alone for red, rosé and sparkling wine. Vegoritis Winery stands on the outskirts of the village, among the lakes and below Mount Voras, called Kaimaktsalan, and takes its name from Lake Vegoritida beside its vineyards. By its own description it joins traditional methods with modern equipment. The regional tourism body lists it among the wineries of Amyntaio open to visitors, who walk the vineyard, tour the cellar and taste over the water. Its Xinomavro is a PDO red of the grape alone from the village's vineyards, given a year in oak barrels and a year in bottle before release; a Greek wine magazine published a note on its 2019 vintage in 2024. It is a house written about in Greece and little seen abroad, and for a sommelier it is the village wine of Amyndeon: plain Xinomavro of the plateau.
